ABSOLUTE PRIORITY — SUBJECT LIKENESS & IDENTITY:
The main subject(s) in the attached photo must remain 100% faithful and instantly recognizable. Likeness and accurate silhouettes matter more than decoration.

Identify the real subject(s) in the photo accurately:
- People: Count every person in the foreground/midground and draw every single one with no one omitted, merged, duplicated, or invented. Preserve each person's exact face shape, eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, real natural expression (do not force a smile or alter emotion), hairstyle, hair length, parting, bangs, beard, glasses (exact frame shape), real worn accessories (caps, hats, headbands, bows, hair clips, earrings), apparent age, and authentic child or adult body proportions (such as a toddler's round cheeks and larger head-to-body ratio). Never beautify, idealize, slim, age, or cartoon-distort faces. Keep exact relative positions, poses, and heights. Omit blurry accidental strangers far in the background.
- Animals & pets: Preserve exact species and breed, ear/muzzle/tail shape, pose, proportions, and distinct coat or fur color-patch boundaries (outline light vs. dark patches with clean closed lines without filling dark patches in black or scribbles).
- Toys, plushies, dolls & vehicles: Render as an original, simplified hand-drawn children's coloring-book outline capturing the physical toy's silhouette, proportions, and main structural features. STRICT PACKAGING & BRAND CLEANUP: Completely omit all retail cardboard boxes, blister packaging, plastic windows, fabric or price hangtags, barcodes, brand logos, trademarked emblems, and printed text, letters, or numbers (leave toy blocks, signs, and vehicle sides free of text or logos). If a toy appears next to or in front of its retail box, draw ONLY the standalone physical toy once—never draw the box or duplicate illustrations from packaging.
- Landscapes & places: Preserve the recognizable composition, horizon, landmarks, and natural or architectural silhouettes cleanly without inventing extra people.

PRINTABLE COLORING PAGE — INK & LINE RULES:
- Pure solid black outlines (#000000) on a pure white (#FFFFFF) background ONLY.
- Zero grey lines, zero faint or semi-transparent background strokes, zero shading, zero gradients, zero cross-hatching, zero stippling/dot-speckles, zero sketchy double-lines, and zero large solid black filled areas. Render dark hair, dark fur, dark clothing, tyres, and animal eyes as open white colorable shapes with crisp black outlines (keep small white catchlight circles inside pupils so eyes look lively, never solid black holes).
- Every coloring region must be a clean, fully closed shape suitable for crayons, markers, or colored pencils. Group micro-textures (individual fur hairs, yarn twists, grass blades, dense leaves, brick/stud grids, fabric weave) into smooth, simplified, child-friendly colorable shapes instead of tiny speckles or hairline strokes.
- Composition: vertical 3:4 portrait page. Frame the main subject(s) prominently as the grounded hero (about 60-75% of page height) with balanced breathing space and a clean white margin around all edges so nothing important is clipped when printed on A4. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, frames, or watermarks anywhere.

FAITHFUL PHOTO MODE (NO FANTASY THEME): Translate ONLY the real subject(s), their real pose, their real clothing and worn accessories, and the essential real-world setting from the attached photo into a clean, joyful coloring page.
- Smart background cleanup: If the photo was taken indoors against messy household clutter, shelves, cables, retail boxes, or a plain studio surface, replace the distracting clutter with clean open white space, a simple grounding surface line, and only the 1-2 real foreground objects the subject is directly touching or playing with. If the photo shows a meaningful outdoor or travel setting (beach, garden, park, mountain, street, landmark), keep that real place recognizable using simplified, bold, uncluttered shapes in crisp solid black lines (never faint grey) that stay visually subordinate and never overpower the main subject.
- Child-friendly clarity: Use bold, smooth outer contours and clean medium inner lines with generous medium-to-large closed coloring areas (simplify dense foliage, knit/yarn strands, tiny polka dots, and complex patterns into clear colorable shapes).
- Strict fidelity guard: DO NOT invent or add any fantasy theme, pirates, ships, unicorns, dragons, knights, space rockets, aliens, dinosaurs, castles, crowns, costume changes, newly invented hats, or imaginary creatures/props not present in the photo.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, frames, or watermarks anywhere.

CREATIVE FANTASY MODE: Keep the main subject(s) from the photo 100% recognizable as the grounded foreground hero (55-75% of page height), standing or sitting naturally on a coherent foreground surface.
- Head, face & real accessories protection: Faces, hair, and animal/toy heads must remain completely clear and unobstructed. Preserve any real glasses, baseball caps, hats, bows, or headbands already worn in the original photo, while NEVER adding newly invented helmets, hats, masks, crowns, tiaras, or overlapping props onto anyone's head or face.
- Subject-aware staging: If people appear in the photo, adapt only their body outfit below the neck into a simple, comfortable themed costume while keeping their real head, hair, worn cap/glasses, pose, and any held object recognizable. If animals, pets, plushies, dolls, or toy vehicles are the subject (with no people in the photo), keep their exact physical form intact—do NOT dress animals or toys in human clothes and do NOT invent imaginary human characters—and stage them naturally as the hero inside the themed world. If a landscape is the subject, weave the themed elements harmoniously into the real scenery.
- Scale background prop count and detail strictly according to the AGE COMPLEXITY level below. Theme: Fairytale kingdom. Ground the subject on a garden courtyard path. If people appear in the photo, dress them in a simple royal gown, tunic, or cape (never add crowns, tiaras, or veils onto heads; keep real hair and any real cap/headband from the photo untouched). Core scene elements: a storybook castle with flags in the background and cheerful garden flowers. Optional secondary details for older age groups: a pumpkin carriage or friendly pony nearby, a simple fountain, and butterflies.

AGE COMPLEXITY (3-4 years / preschool): Bold, smooth, clear outlines with large friendly coloring areas and uncluttered spacing. Include the main subject plus 2-3 clear core theme elements; keep clothing and backgrounds simple without small decorative patterns.
